ca.title: Finding hope beyond addiction: Teen Challenge supports women in recovery
ca.description: Some of the women in Adult and Teen Challenge in-residence program in Brandon. (Adult and Teen Challenge Central Canada/Facebook) After years of connecting with women battling addiction behind prison walls, one Adult & Teen Challenge staff member is continuing that work in a new way, helping women in Brandon find hope and build a new life through faith and recovery. "Before moving to Brandon, I worked out of Winnipeg's community office," says Davis, a staff member at Adult and Teen Challenge Central Canada. "Out of there, I helped individuals who were applying to the program." Davis' job included connecting with women who were currently incarcerated in Manitoba. Davis enjoyed connecting with women inmates on a heart level about many different things, including faith, life struggles, and addiction. "We go into many different correctional institutions across central Canada. We might hold chapels and we might hold these different outpatient groups, and different kinds of activities where we can engage people in different units. That's the place where anyone of any kind of stage of recovery is welcome to join." From the relationships built through this work, many women leave prison and continue the community support groups once a week. A few even realize that they need further help, which ATC can offer in-residence recovery support in Brandon for women. "We'll talk about grief and how that does affect or can be impacted by addiction. We talk about healthy relationships and how to build and recognize those. How to create action plans for different situations or emotions. A new role, yet continuing work with women in recovery Davis recently moved to Brandon, switching into a different role. She is now a program coordinator for women battling addiction and recovering in their in-residence program. "A lot of women have struggled with addiction for a long time," says Davis. "That can become their only known identity. Their world revolves around it." Adult & Teen Challenge offers a wholistic approach to addiction recovery, bringing in a deep-rooted faith in Jesus Christ, alongside a strict routine and boundaries. "I see women in our program start to have hope. I think hope is such a key thing in this program and with God. Hope for a better life, hope that leads me to change, and hope that keeps me steadfast in challenge. When someone is able to latch onto hope in Christ, that's where transformation begins." Anyone interested in hearing more stories of transformation and change can tune in to the Be Part of a Story radiothon, Dec. 8-10, in support of Adult & Teen Challenge. CHVN will be live on location all three days, from 6 a.m. until 6 p.m.

in.title: Sports Min Mandaviya to lead 100th Fit India Sundays on Cycle from Pune
in.description: New Delhi, Nov 27 (IANS) Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya will lead the celebrations of the 100th edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle in Pune on November 29, with around 50,000 cycling enthusiasts expected to participate in the landmark event. The milestone edition of the nationwide fitness initiative will be celebrated under the theme #IndiaReadyForOlympics, highlighting the Olympic Movement and India’s efforts to strengthen its sporting culture. The celebrations will also see 100 Indian Olympians participate at 100 prominent locations across the country, while young people from every district will join the movement in association with MY Bharat. Mandaviya will lead the main event from Pimpri-Chinchwad in Pune, where thousands of participants are expected to come together to promote cycling and encourage fitness as part of their daily routine. Launched in December 2024 following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for a fitter and healthier nation, Fit India Sundays on Cycle has evolved into a nationwide people’s movement. The initiative, which began with 250 locations and around 500 participants in New Delhi, has expanded significantly over the last two years. Custom Ad: Multiplex Its 99th edition, organised around the theme of Constitution Day, witnessed participation by lakhs of citizens at more than 26,000 locations across the country, reflecting the growing reach of the fitness campaign. The 100th edition will also focus on the core values of the Olympic Movement, including good governance, integrity, fair competition, inclusion, athlete welfare and sustainability. It aims to encourage greater awareness about ethical sporting practices, equal opportunities and the importance of providing a safe environment for athletes. The celebrations will underline India’s commitment to building a sporting ecosystem that gives importance to athlete voices and inclusivity, with particular emphasis on women and para-athletes. The initiative also seeks to inspire young people to embrace sports and physical activity as an integral part of their lives. The campaign draws inspiration from the Prime Minister’s message, “Fitness ka Dose, Aadha Ghanta Roz”, encouraging citizens to dedicate at least 30 minutes every day to physical activity. Over the course of its journey, Sundays on Cycle has also emerged as a platform to promote wider national campaigns and social messages through public participation. Special editions have focused on themes such as the fight against obesity, Nasha Mukt Bharat and Pollution Ka Solution, encouraging citizens to adopt healthier habits and contribute towards the vision of a Fit India and Viksit Bharat. --IANS sds/

sg.title: Chengdu: Where poetry flows through everyday life
sg.description: BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A report from People's Daily -- German poet and painter Margarete Werner reads at home. (Photo/Dai Guangyu) The Minjiang River has carved its path through the landscape for millennia, but it was human ingenuity that truly tamed it. The Dujiangyan irrigation system, engineered over two thousand years ago in southwest China's Sichuan province, channels the river's waters across the fertile Chengdu Plain. For centuries, this marvel of hydraulic engineering has shielded the region from catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, laying the foundation for what became known as the "Land of Abundance." Long before modern infrastructure, Sichuan attracted scholars and poets, earning the enduring belief that the land itself inspires verse. Chengdu holds a rare distinction in Chinese history: it has occupied the same site and kept the same name for roughly three thousand years. Today, it stands as a living testament to this continuity -- a metropolis where deep-rooted traditions and dynamic innovation thrive side by side. Nestled among the misty peaks of Qingcheng Mountain, a quiet cottage belongs to Margarete Werner, a German painter and poet who goes by the Chinese name Lei Zhen. Inside, floor-to-ceiling shelves hold Chinese classics alongside Western literary works, reflecting a mind shaped by two cultures. Surrounded by emerald hills and terraced tea gardens, she finds inspiration at the intersection of Eastern and Western thought. Werner grew up in the foothills of the Alps. Ink and wash paintings collected by her grandmother first introduced her to the aesthetics of the East. At 19, while studying in London, she happened upon Chinese classics in a bookstore in Chinatown. From then on, she felt drawn to this distant land. After graduation, she moved to China, eventually settling on Qingcheng Mountain with her husband to focus fully on her writing. "I've always felt that Li Bai is a profoundly universal poet. His verses speak directly to the human experience, transcending time and borders," she said. She often recites poetry while hiking mountain trails. One line from Li Bai's Dulu Pian resonates deeply with her: "A bright moon shines straight down, revealing all without concealment." Its unguarded honesty mirrors the tranquil, grounded life she has cultivated here. Sichuan has long had a close connection with poetry. Famous Chinese poets Du Fu, Li Bai, and Lu You all composed celebrated works in Chengdu, helping shape the city's cultural character. For Werner, however, the city's poetic spirit is not confined to the pages of books. It is also alive in everyday speech. Residents still use words like luo yu (falling rain) and niao huan (birds singing), preserving the musicality of ancient Chinese in daily conversation. "Standing at the foot of Qingcheng Mountain, I feel that the rhythms of Tang and Song poetry have returned to their original form," Werner said. This poetic atmosphere extends beyond literature. Since the launch of the Chengdu International Poetry Week in 2017, more than 110 foreign poets from over 50 countries and regions have visited the city to seek inspiration. Their works offer glimpses of Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets, with some featured in a collection titled "A city in the depths of time: Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets." To Werner, "poetry is like green bamboo, with the vitality to pierce through concrete."

th.description: อนุบาลแพร่สุดภูมิใจ! คว้ารางวัลระดับประเทศ EGAT Green Learning Society Awards 2026 ยกระดับสถานศึกษาสู่สังคมแห่งการเรียนรู้สีเขียว โรงเรียนอนุบาลแพร่ สังกัดสำนักงานเขตพื้นที่การศึกษาประถมศึกษาแพร่ เขต 1 สร้างความภาคภูมิใจ คว้ารางวัลระดับประเทศ EGAT Green Learning Society Awards 2026 จากการไฟฟ้าฝ่ายผลิตแห่งประเทศไทย (กฟผ.) ร่วมกับสำนักงานคณะกรรมการการศึกษาขั้นพื้นฐาน (สพฐ.) สะท้อนความมุ่งมั่นในการส่งเสริมการเรียนรู้และสร้างสังคมที่ใส่ใจสิ่งแวดล้อมอย่างยั่งยืน เมื่อวันศุกร์ที่ 27 พฤศจิกายน 2569 การไฟฟ้าฝ่ายผลิตแห่งประเทศไทย (กฟผ.) ร่วมกับสำนักงานคณะกรรมการการศึกษาขั้นพื้นฐาน จัดพิธีมอบรางวัล EGAT Green Learning Society Awards 2026 โดยมีนายวฤต รัตนชื่น รองผู้ว่าการยุทธศาสตร์ การไฟฟ้าฝ่ายผลิตแห่งประเทศไทย เป็นประธานในพิธีมอบรางวัล ขณะที่ ดร.อรุณี จิรมหาศาล ผู้ช่วยเลขาธิการคณะกรรมการการศึกษาขั้นพื้นฐาน กล่าวขอบคุณผู้เกี่ยวข้อง ในการนี้ โรงเรียนอนุบาลแพร่ นำโดยนายชาญณรงค์ จันทร์ป้อม ผู้อำนวยการโรงเรียนอนุบาลแพร่ […] Source

th.description: โครงสร้างการแข่งขันในธุรกิจอีคอมเมิร์ซไทยกำลังเข้าสู่การกำกับดูแลที่เข้มข้นขึ้น หลังสำนักงานคณะกรรมการการแข่งขันทางการค้า (กขค.) เดินหน้าตรวจสอบระบบจัดสรรงานขนส่งของแพลตฟอร์มรายใหญ่ พร้อมผลักดันร่างหลักเกณฑ์กำกับการจัดส่งสินค้าในระบบนิเวศแพลตฟอร์ม มุ่งป้องกันการบังคับร้านค้าใช้บริการขนส่งรายใดรายหนึ่ง และลดพฤติกรรมเลือกปฏิบัติต่อผู้ให้บริการรายอื่น ความเคลื่อนไหวดังกล่าวเป็นประเด็นที่ผู้ประกอบการ SME ในภาคเหนือควรติดตาม เนื่องจากการเข้าถึงช่องทางจำหน่ายและบริการขนส่งเป็นองค์ประกอบสำคัญของต้นทุนและความสามารถในการแข่งขันของธุรกิจออนไลน์ ความเคลื่อนไหวดังกล่าวแสดงให้เห็นถึงแนวทางของภาครัฐในการยกระดับการแข่งขันทางการค้า ลดภาระต้นทุน และเพิ่มโอกาสให้ผู้ประกอบการรายย่อยสามารถแข่งขันได้อย่างเป็นธรรม โดยสาระสำคัญของร่างประกาศฉบับใหม่ คือการรับรองสิทธิของร้านค้าและผู้ซื้อในการเลือกผู้ให้บริการขนส่งได้อย่างอิสระ ร้านค้าสามารถใช้บริการขนส่งของตนเองหรือเลือกผู้ให้บริการภายนอกแพลตฟอร์มได้ ขณะที่แพลตฟอร์มจะไม่สามารถบังคับให้ใช้บริษัทขนส่งในเครือหรือพันธมิตรทางธุรกิจเพื่อแลกกับสิทธิประโยชน์ในการขายสินค้า รวมถึงไม่ควรใช้มาตรการตอบโต้ร้านค้าที่เลือกขนส่งรายอื่น เช่น ลดอันดับการแสดงผลสินค้า เพิ่มค่าธรรมเนียม หรือตัดสิทธิประโยชน์ทางการค้า ขณะเดียวกัน กขค.อยู่ระหว่างขอข้อมูลจากแพลตฟอร์มรายใหญ่ เพื่อตรวจสอบสัดส่วนคำสั่งซื้อและปริมาณพัสดุที่จัดสรรให้บริษัทขนส่งแต่ละราย ว่ามีการกระจุกตัวหรือเอื้อประโยชน์ให้ผู้ให้บริการบางรายอย่างไม่เป็นธรรมหรือไม่ โดยใช้หลัก FRAND (Fair, Reasonable and Non-Discriminatory) ซึ่งประกอบด้วยความเป็นธรรม ความสมเหตุสมผล และการไม่เลือกปฏิบัติ เป็นกรอบในการพิจารณา ประเด็นนี้มีความสำคัญต่อการแข่งขันในธุรกิจโลจิสติกส์ โดยเฉพาะผู้ให้บริการรายเล็กและรายใหม่ที่ต้องการเข้าถึงงานจากแพลตฟอร์ม หากการจัดสรรคำสั่งซื้อไม่เป็นธรรม ย่อมส่งผลต่อโอกาสในการแข่งขันทั้งด้านราคาและคุณภาพบริการ ด้านการบังคับใช้กฎหมาย หากตรวจพบว่าแพลตฟอร์มใช้อำนาจเหนือตลาดโดยมิชอบ อาจเข้าข่ายความผิดตามพระราชบัญญัติการแข่งขันทางการค้า พ.ศ. 2560 มาตรา 50 ซึ่งมีโทษจำคุกไม่เกิน 2 ปี หรือปรับไม่เกิน 10% ของรายได้ในปีที่กระทำความผิด หรือทั้งจำทั้งปรับ […] Source

ph.title: Rent-to-own program makes rooftop solar accessible to Filipino homes, small businesses
ph.description: Adopting residential solar has opened up new opportunities for households and businesses, giving them more control over their power consumption while also reducing costs. Before rooftop solar, early movers were also typical customers who were cutting down on their electricity use, worried about getting a shock on their utility bill. “Matagal ko nang gusto talagang mag-solar panel. Pero long-term commitment ito eh. So kailangan kong pag-isipan talaga yung company or kung sino yung magkakabit. Gustong-gusto ko dahil sa sobrang taas ng [electricity bill] ko – [rooftop solar] yung isang naisip ko kung paano mapababa,” shared Grace Gozarin, a residential customer from Tanza, Cavite. [I’ve really wanted to get solar panels for a long time. But it’s a long-term commitment, so I need to carefully consider which company or who exactly will handle the installation. I’m very keen on it because my electricity bill is so high. I thought of rooftop solar as an option to help lower those costs.] The Gozarin household, like many captive customers, had to dig deep into their pockets, even when they already compromised their consumption. In fact, Filipinos pay for one of the most expensive electricity in Southeast Asia, while also having one of the lowest power consumption per capita in the region. “Yung pagtitipid usually nagagawa namin sa aircon. Kapag alam naming tumataas ang [presyo ng kuryente], patayin muna ang aircon,” she explained. “Minsan nga iniisip ko kung gusto ko maglagay ng mga Christmas lights. Pero ‘pag iniisip ko yung kuryente parang napapatigil ako. Kailangan ko ba?” [We usually save by cutting back on air conditioning. When we know that electricity prices are going up, we just turn off the air conditioner. Sometimes, I even consider putting up Christmas lights — but then I think about the electricity cost, and I hesitate. Do I really need them?] This has changed for Mrs. Gozarin and her family when they tapped Solviva Energy and took advantage of its zero-down payment and rent-to-own plan. The Christmas lights are now up Solviva Energy is a residential solar startup under 1882 Energy Ventures, the startup and innovation arm of Aboitiz Power Corporation (AboitizPower), serving as a direct-to-consumer bridge for clean energy solutions since 2023. “When we looked into solar for households, we saw that there are two major barriers: the upfront cost and trust,” said Solviva Energy CEO Coby Cobankiat. “This is a segment that, historically, has been served by smaller players. With that, customer experience is inconsistent, you don’t really know who’s installing for you, and you don’t know if it’s compliant.” “Trust is such a big thing, especially for a system that’s gonna last 25 years or more,” he maintained. To address these prevailing challenges to adoption, Solviva Energy launched its rent-to-own program in 2025, complete with an end-to-end service that includes site assessments and after-sales support throughout a system’s operational life. “Rent-to-own is up to five years to pay, zero down payment. Customers have one full month of savings, and only then do we ask them to pay for their first bill. So you can actually use your savings to pay for your monthly installment with Solviva,” Cobankiat explained. The benefits of residential solar to the Gozarin family were immediate as they saw a significant drop in their electricity bills after installation. “Yung rent-to-own, nagulat ako na may ganun pala na opportunity para sa mga simpleng tao. Kaya pala natin magkaroon ng solar,” Mrs. Gozarin said. “Ngayon po na nakakatipid na kami nang ganto, nadagdag namin sa savings ng bahay at sa emergency fund.” [I was surprised to learn about the ‘rent-to-own’ option — I didn’t realize such an opportunity existed for ordinary people. It turns out we can actually have solar power. Now that we’re saving this much, we’ve been able to add to our household savings and our emergency fund.] “Sobrang worth it. Ngayon mayroon na akong Christmas decor. Hindi na po ako nagi-guilty na maglagay ng Christmas lights sa labas kase nakakatipid na kami sa kuryente,” she added. [It’s so worth it. Now I have Christmas decorations. I no longer feel guilty about putting up Christmas lights outside because we’re saving on electricity.] Solar savings fuel campus upgrades Christmas also came early for Lord’s Hand Academy, a private school in Pasig City, with savings from solar panels clearing the way for infrastructural and operational improvements. ph.title: Property sector to rebound from high interest rates, condo oversupply in 2027
ph.description: CEBU CITY – High interest rates and condominium oversupply hounded the property sector this year and will remain a challenge next year. But for an award-winning developer, sustained demand from end-user buyers is keeping growth alive for developers heading into 2027. According to Federal Land Inc. President Jose Mari Banzon, the company has outperformed its previous year's sales figures, driven largely by individuals purchasing homes to live in rather than speculative investors. While steep borrowing costs have sidelined investor-driven acquisitions, promotional offers and flexible payment terms continue to draw owner-occupiers into the market. “Even with talk of an oversupply and sluggish sales, we are actually exceeding last year's figures, so we are growing,” Banzon told reporters during a media briefing on Thursday, Nov. 26. He noted that end-users will remain the primary growth engine for the residential sector in 2027, provided developers deliver quality projects paired with competitive pricing and attainable payment structures. Capitalizing on this momentum, Federal Land is ramping up the development of its eight-hectare Marco Polo estate in Cebu City, with plans to introduce new retail spaces and upscale residential towers. The sprawling property already anchors Marco Polo Plaza Cebu and Marco Polo Residences – the developer's first branded residential enclave in the city. The first four condominium towers at Marco Polo Residences are completely sold out, while construction is actively underway on the fifth tower alongside an initial commercial building slated for completion next year. To develop the estate’s remaining footprint, Federal Land will tap the Federal Land Nomura Group (FNG), its joint venture with Japanese real estate giant Nomura Real Estate. Banzon noted that FNG will bring the same luxury pedigree behind its flagship Metro Manila projects, The Estate Makati, Grand Hyatt Residences in Bonifacio Global City, and The Seasons Residences, to Cebu, leveraging the hillside estate’s elevated vantage point and panoramic city views. Banzon gave his projections after leading the annual Christmas tree lighting ceremony of Marco Polo Plaza Cebu. It was also during the event that Federal Land celebrated winning the Developer of the Year award during the 2026 Philippine Real Estate Awards in September. Marco Polo Residences also took home the Best Investment Property in Metro Cebu accolade. “We are grateful for these recognitions as they reflect the hard work of our people and the trust our partners and customers have placed in us over the years,” said Banzon.

ph.title: Chengdu: Where poetry flows through everyday life
ph.description: BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A report from People's Daily -- German poet and painter Margarete Werner reads at home. (Photo/Dai Guangyu) The Minjiang River has carved its path through the landscape for millennia, but it was human ingenuity that truly tamed it. The Dujiangyan irrigation system, engineered over two thousand years ago in southwest China's Sichuan province, channels the river's waters across the fertile Chengdu Plain. For centuries, this marvel of hydraulic engineering has shielded the region from catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, laying the foundation for what became known as the "Land of Abundance." Long before modern infrastructure, Sichuan attracted scholars and poets, earning the enduring belief that the land itself inspires verse. Chengdu holds a rare distinction in Chinese history: it has occupied the same site and kept the same name for roughly three thousand years. Today, it stands as a living testament to this continuity -- a metropolis where deep-rooted traditions and dynamic innovation thrive side by side. Nestled among the misty peaks of Qingcheng Mountain, a quiet cottage belongs to Margarete Werner, a German painter and poet who goes by the Chinese name Lei Zhen. Inside, floor-to-ceiling shelves hold Chinese classics alongside Western literary works, reflecting a mind shaped by two cultures. Surrounded by emerald hills and terraced tea gardens, she finds inspiration at the intersection of Eastern and Western thought. Werner grew up in the foothills of the Alps. Ink and wash paintings collected by her grandmother first introduced her to the aesthetics of the East. At 19, while studying in London, she happened upon Chinese classics in a bookstore in Chinatown. From then on, she felt drawn to this distant land. After graduation, she moved to China, eventually settling on Qingcheng Mountain with her husband to focus fully on her writing. "I've always felt that Li Bai is a profoundly universal poet. His verses speak directly to the human experience, transcending time and borders," she said. She often recites poetry while hiking mountain trails. One line from Li Bai's Dulu Pian resonates deeply with her: "A bright moon shines straight down, revealing all without concealment." Its unguarded honesty mirrors the tranquil, grounded life she has cultivated here. Sichuan has long had a close connection with poetry. Famous Chinese poets Du Fu, Li Bai, and Lu You all composed celebrated works in Chengdu, helping shape the city's cultural character. For Werner, however, the city's poetic spirit is not confined to the pages of books. It is also alive in everyday speech. Residents still use words like luo yu (falling rain) and niao huan (birds singing), preserving the musicality of ancient Chinese in daily conversation. "Standing at the foot of Qingcheng Mountain, I feel that the rhythms of Tang and Song poetry have returned to their original form," Werner said. This poetic atmosphere extends beyond literature. Since the launch of the Chengdu International Poetry Week in 2017, more than 110 foreign poets from over 50 countries and regions have visited the city to seek inspiration. Their works offer glimpses of Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets, with some featured in a collection titled "A city in the depths of time: Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets." To Werner, "poetry is like green bamboo, with the vitality to pierce through concrete."

ph.title: Chula Engineering's DIY X-Ray Imaging Device Using a Phosphor Screen and Plywood Box to Screen Bags and Parcels for Suspicious Objects
ph.description: BANGKOK, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, millions of parcels pass through postal services and private delivery companies as online shopping continues to grow. Yet their contents are often unknown, raising concerns about concealed weapons and other dangerous items. How can bags and parcels be screened widely without relying on imported X-ray machines that cost millions of baht and are mainly available at international airports and other high-security locations? DIY X-Ray Imaging Device A team from the Department of Nuclear Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Chulalongkorn University, comprising Assoc. Prof. Nares Chankow, Dr. Dhanut Saengchantra, Mr. Phongyuth Sriploy, Mr. Prathan Mirattanaprai, and Miss Siripreeya Pipatpunlop, offers a solution to this dilemma. The team designed and built an entire X-ray and gamma-ray imaging device based on the physical phenomena of fluoroscopy in combination with a modern-day digital camera using a simple but effective approach: combining a nearly century-old physics principle with an ordinary digital camera. The resulting device can screen bags and parcels at a fraction of the cost of commercial X-ray machines. How the Idea Began The idea behind the X-ray device was straightforward. Assoc. Prof. Nares explained that imaging with 'phosphor screens'—sheets that glow when exposed to radiation—has been around for nearly a century. Newer radiographic technologies offering higher resolution have largely replaced this method, but its key advantage remains, namely that it is less costly. Meanwhile, digital cameras have advanced considerably, producing sharper images, and their connection to computers makes image adjustments easier. Bringing the two technologies together offers opportunity in solving the problem of screening parcels and packages. Today, phosphor screens are used mainly in medical imaging of the human body. The Department of Nuclear Engineering's research team, however, saw another application: inspecting bags and parcels for concealed explosives, firearms, and other illegal items. This serves a very different purpose from medical imaging, and few have pursued building such equipment themselves. In 2011, the team designed and assembled an X-ray imaging device and supplied it to the Fine Arts Department to examine artifacts in the National Museums without damaging these historically valuable objects. The device remains in use today and has since been adapted to produce three-dimensional images. It takes two images from left and right positions separated by approximately the distance between human eyes. Then two images are displayed on a 3D television to reveal depth. The principle mirrors human vision: each eye sees a slightly different view; the brain combines them into a single 3D image. How the Device Works Assoc. Prof. Nares explained that when X-rays or gamma rays pass through an object, the amount of radiation that emerges varies according to the thickness and type of material of the object. When this radiation reaches the phosphor screen, the screen glows with varying brightness. Areas receiving more radiation appear brighter, while those where dense objects block the radiation appear darker. He compared this to "Nang Talung" or "Thai shadow puppetry," in which light from behind the puppets creates contrasting dark silhouettes and bright areas that reveal their shapes. A digital camera takes a picture of the light-and-dark image on the phosphor screen. Assoc. Prof. Nares noted that the camera must avoid direct exposure to radiation, which would interact with its image sensor—whether a CCD (charge-coupled device) or CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor)—and introduce image noise. To address this, the team installed a mirror at a 45-degree angle inside the enclosure. The mirror reflects the screen's image toward a camera positioned away from the direct path of the radiation. All these components are housed in an L-shaped, lightproof plywood box designed and built by the team. The phosphor screen is mounted at the front, with an aluminum sheet covering it to prevent outside light from interfering with the image. The digital camera sits in a separate compartment within the same box, capturing the reflected image and sending it to a laptop screen in real time. Operators can quickly view, adjust, and analyze the images without developing film as in traditional X-ray imaging. Cost: A Key Advantage The clearest difference between this device and airport baggage scanners or medical X-ray machines is the price. Commercial X-ray machines that use a single row of radiation detectors to scan an image section by section and assemble the results cost millions of baht. By comparison, the materials and components for the Chula team's X-ray imaging device cost no more than 50,000 baht, excluding the separate X-ray generator, which costs around one million baht. The gamma-ray imaging version costs no more than 80,000 baht, excluding the radiation source. These imaging devices therefore cost a fraction of a complete imported X-ray system, although the radiation source must be purchased separately. Imaging Performance Assoc. Prof. Nares emphasized that the device is not intended to match the image resolution of medical X-ray machines or equipment used to detect tiny cracks or air pockets in metal castings. Such applications require exceptionally detailed images. For security screening of bags and parcels, however, the aim is to distinguish the shapes of concealed objects and determine whether they resemble firearms, ammunition, or bags containing suspicious items. This level of detail can be achieved with inexpensive, standard phosphor screens and a midrange camera, keeping costs much lower while still meeting practical screening needs. The device also matches commercial machines in speed, taking just 10–30 seconds to image a parcel. Airport X-ray scanners, by contrast, move baggage past a single row of radiation detectors, capturing successive sections and assembling them into an image. Imaging time can be reduced further by increasing the camera's sensitivity setting or the radiation intensity, although this may slightly reduce image detail. Operational Safety Assoc. Prof. Nares explained that the radiation used in this imaging system has relatively low energy, making suitable shielding reasonably straightforward to design. The differences between X-rays and gamma rays are explained below. X-rays are produced by an electrically powered generator, making them easier to control, and the machine can be switched on when needed and switched off immediately afterward. This makes radiation safety easier to manage. Gamma rays, however, come from radioactive materials that continuously emit radiation and cannot be switched off. When not in use, the gamma-ray source must therefore remain in a specifically designed shielded container. During imaging, the source is temporarily moved out of the container through a guide tube. For practical use, the team proposes a concrete tunnel with a conveyor belt to carry bags and parcels, similar to airport baggage screening systems. This would keep operators away from the irradiation area during operation. With an X-ray system, configuring the generator to operate only during screening would further reduce operators' exposure. Testing with Different Radiation Sources The team tested the device under various conditions, adjusting X-ray and gamma-ray energy levels, camera settings, and exposure times. They also compared two phosphor screens made from the same material, gadolinium oxysulfide, but with different densities: the standard DRZ model and the high-density PI-200 model. The Japanese-made screens can accommodate gamma-ray energies of up to approximately 500 kiloelectron volts (keV). For gamma-ray imaging, the team tested two isotopes: iridium-192, with an average energy of approximately 320 keV and a half-life of 74 days, and selenium-75, with an average energy of approximately 280 keV and a longer half-life of 120 days. Half-life has practical implications: the radiation emitted by the source decreases by half over each half-life, requiring twice the exposure time to obtain an image. Since exposures take only seconds, extending the imaging time is manageable and reduces the need to replace the source frequently. The tests showed that X-rays produced images with good sharpness and contrast. Gamma-ray images from both iridium-192 and selenium-75 were less sharp and had lower contrast but were still clear enough to detect concealed objects inside bags and parcels. The team tested a range of objects, including parcels containing mixed items such as scissors, staplers, and a tennis ball with coins hidden inside. Other test objects included a steel pipe containing stones and steel pieces with concealed drilled holes. In every case, the images revealed the internal shapes clearly enough to determine whether further inspection was needed. Social Impact and Next Steps According to Assoc. Prof. Nares this research addresses two connected needs in Thai society. The first concerns the safety of the general public. With uncertainty about the contents of parcels delivered each day, affordable screening equipment accessible to schools, government offices, and private delivery companies could help reduce the risks posed by concealed dangerous objects. The second concerns the economic benefits. Producing such equipment locally at a fraction of the cost of imported systems would lower costs and give organizations with limited budgets greater access to security screening technology. "Several organizations have already contacted us asking for advice on developing the equipment. Our team is happy to offer guidance or training so that interested organizations can build their own devices, rather than focusing solely on manufacturing them for sale. We believe sharing knowledge will make this technology more widely accessible." – Assoc. Prof. Nares "Some Thai companies have now begun producing key components such as X-ray tubes. With continued support, this could help reduce reliance on imports over the long term," Assoc. Prof. Nares said. He added that, for researchers, the satisfaction of developing an innovation comes from seeing the knowledge and technology passed on and put to good use, rather than selling as many devices as possible. "The best research is research that is put into practice and helps solve society's problems sustainably", he emphasized. Looking ahead, he sees potential applications beyond detecting firearms and ammunition, particularly in food safety screening. These could include detecting foreign materials in food products—a risk that he believes still receives too little public attention. In conclusion, the Chula Team presents this simple, low-cost X-ray imaging device consisting of a phosphor screen, a mirror, a digital camera and an L-shape plywood box. This innovation shows that meeting society's needs does not always require expensive, cutting-edge technology. Sometimes, the answer lies in thoughtfully combining basic nuclear engineering knowledge with readily available equipment. Continue reading a full article on the website: https://www.chula.ac.th/en/highlight/431558/ Chulalongkorn University has been ranked Thailand's No. 1 university for the 17th consecutive year (since 2009) in the newly released QS World University Rankings 2026. The university is ranked 221st in the world and places among the world's Top 100 in two key indicators: Academic Reputation (89th) and Employment Outcomes (64th).

ph.title: GENIUS MACHINERY to Showcase Energy-Saving DWX Film Recycling System at IPF Japan 2026
ph.description: Designed for film recycling, the single-motor DWX targets labor shortages and rising power costs, with energy cost savings of up to 65%. TAICHUNG, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GENIUS MACHINERY, a Taiwan-based manufacturer of plastic recycling equipment, will exhibit its DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine—a compact, all-in-one system specifically engineered for plastic film recycling—at IPF Japan 2026, held from December 1 to 5 at Makuhari Messe in Chiba (Hall 7, Booth 71814). GENIUS will co-exhibit with its long-term Japanese distributor, Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd., and display the DWX system alongside film samples before and after squeezing to demonstrate its dewatering efficiency and volume reduction firsthand. GENIUS DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine for plastic film recycling. Plastic recyclers in Japan—and across most global markets—are facing mounting operational pressures on two fronts: severe labor shortages and continuously rising electricity and fuel costs. For plant operators processing agricultural film, LDPE/HDPE film, and post-consumer flexible packaging, the critical challenge is maintaining high throughput with fewer operators and lower power consumption. To address this, GENIUS developed the DWX series specifically for film applications by combining squeezing and extrusion into a single, compact unit driven by one motor and one screw. Watch the DWX squeezing and extrusion process. Crucially, the DWX retains the core dewatering mechanism of GENIUS's established DW Series Squeeze Dryer—a proven system with over 55 units sold in Japan and widely trusted by local recyclers for years. In existing Japanese post-consumer film operations, the standalone DW technology has consistently reduced outlet moisture from 50% to below 1%, cutting pellet reject rates from 15–20% to under 1%. By integrating this field-proven squeezing stage directly before extrusion, the DWX reduces washed film moisture from over 50% to below 1% in the first stage before feeding it directly into the extruder. This streamlined single-heat process helps avoid repeated melting cycles, reducing thermal degradation of the polymer while avoiding unnecessary energy and resource waste. While upfront equipment price is a one-time expense, ongoing electricity and labor bills are what truly dictate a recycling plant's long-term profitability. That is why GENIUS urges recyclers to look past the initial price tag and evaluate the total cost of ownership. In a recent line-configuration assessment for a Western European PE film recycling group, switching from a traditional three-machine setup (432 kW total installed main-motor power) to a single DWX-3512 class configuration (150 kW) would cut electricity use by an estimated 107,000 kWh a month—based on 24-hour operation, 22 days a month at 80% load and a 0.9 power factor. Overall, GENIUS estimates that the DWX series can deliver energy cost savings of up to 65%, with one to two operators able to manage the entire line. (Note: Actual savings vary depending on local electricity rates, material types, initial moisture, and throughput.) "Japanese recyclers are among the most quality-conscious in the world, and they demand verifiable performance rather than mere estimates," said Peter Tsai, CEO of GENIUS MACHINERY. "By building the DWX directly on the proven dewatering core of our DW series, we are giving film recyclers a reliable way to cut power bills and simplify staffing without compromising pellet quality. We invite visitors to our booth at IPF Japan to inspect the machine and verify our numbers line by line." Visitors to Hall 7, Booth 71814 can consult directly with technical specialists from GENIUS MACHINERY and Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd. for customized cost-of-ownership evaluations and material testing. About GENIUS MACHINERY Founded in 1975 and headquartered in Taichung, Taiwan, GENIUS MACHINERY specializes in plastic recycling machinery. Its product lineup—including the DW Plastic Squeeze Dryer and the DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine—processes agricultural film, post-consumer film, and flexible packaging waste. With over 2,000 installations across 50 countries, GENIUS provides localized sales and technical support in Japan through Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd. Meanwhile, digital cameras have advanced considerably, producing sharper images, and their connection to computers makes image adjustments easier. Bringing the two technologies together offers opportunity in solving the problem of screening parcels and packages. Today, phosphor screens are used mainly in medical imaging of the human body. The Department of Nuclear Engineering's research team, however, saw another application: inspecting bags and parcels for concealed explosives, firearms, and other illegal items. This serves a very different purpose from medical imaging, and few have pursued building such equipment themselves. In 2011, the team designed and assembled an X-ray imaging device and supplied it to the Fine Arts Department to examine artifacts in the National Museums without damaging these historically valuable objects. The device remains in use today and has since been adapted to produce three-dimensional images. It takes two images from left and right positions separated by approximately the distance between human eyes. Then two images are displayed on a 3D television to reveal depth. The principle mirrors human vision: each eye sees a slightly different view; the brain combines them into a single 3D image. How the Device Works Assoc. Prof. Nares explained that when X-rays or gamma rays pass through an object, the amount of radiation that emerges varies according to the thickness and type of material of the object. When this radiation reaches the phosphor screen, the screen glows with varying brightness. Areas receiving more radiation appear brighter, while those where dense objects block the radiation appear darker. He compared this to "Nang Talung" or "Thai shadow puppetry," in which light from behind the puppets creates contrasting dark silhouettes and bright areas that reveal their shapes. A digital camera takes a picture of the light-and-dark image on the phosphor screen. Assoc. Prof. Nares noted that the camera must avoid direct exposure to radiation, which would interact with its image sensor—whether a CCD (charge-coupled device) or CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor)—and introduce image noise. To address this, the team installed a mirror at a 45-degree angle inside the enclosure. The mirror reflects the screen's image toward a camera positioned away from the direct path of the radiation. All these components are housed in an L-shaped, lightproof plywood box designed and built by the team. The phosphor screen is mounted at the front, with an aluminum sheet covering it to prevent outside light from interfering with the image. The digital camera sits in a separate compartment within the same box, capturing the reflected image and sending it to a laptop screen in real time. Operators can quickly view, adjust, and analyze the images without developing film as in traditional X-ray imaging. Cost: A Key Advantage The clearest difference between this device and airport baggage scanners or medical X-ray machines is the price. Commercial X-ray machines that use a single row of radiation detectors to scan an image section by section and assemble the results cost millions of baht. By comparison, the materials and components for the Chula team's X-ray imaging device cost no more than 50,000 baht, excluding the separate X-ray generator, which costs around one million baht. The gamma-ray imaging version costs no more than 80,000 baht, excluding the radiation source. These imaging devices therefore cost a fraction of a complete imported X-ray system, although the radiation source must be purchased separately. Imaging Performance Assoc. Prof. Nares emphasized that the device is not intended to match the image resolution of medical X-ray machines or equipment used to detect tiny cracks or air pockets in metal castings. Such applications require exceptionally detailed images. For security screening of bags and parcels, however, the aim is to distinguish the shapes of concealed objects and determine whether they resemble firearms, ammunition, or bags containing suspicious items. This level of detail can be achieved with inexpensive, standard phosphor screens and a midrange camera, keeping costs much lower while still meeting practical screening needs. The device also matches commercial machines in speed, taking just 10–30 seconds to image a parcel. Airport X-ray scanners, by contrast, move baggage past a single row of radiation detectors, capturing successive sections and assembling them into an image. Imaging time can be reduced further by increasing the camera's sensitivity setting or the radiation intensity, although this may slightly reduce image detail. Operational Safety Assoc. Prof. Nares explained that the radiation used in this imaging system has relatively low energy, making suitable shielding reasonably straightforward to design. The differences between X-rays and gamma rays are explained below. X-rays are produced by an electrically powered generator, making them easier to control, and the machine can be switched on when needed and switched off immediately afterward. This makes radiation safety easier to manage. Gamma rays, however, come from radioactive materials that continuously emit radiation and cannot be switched off. When not in use, the gamma-ray source must therefore remain in a specifically designed shielded container. During imaging, the source is temporarily moved out of the container through a guide tube. For practical use, the team proposes a concrete tunnel with a conveyor belt to carry bags and parcels, similar to airport baggage screening systems. This would keep operators away from the irradiation area during operation. With an X-ray system, configuring the generator to operate only during screening would further reduce operators' exposure. Testing with Different Radiation Sources The team tested the device under various conditions, adjusting X-ray and gamma-ray energy levels, camera settings, and exposure times. They also compared two phosphor screens made from the same material, gadolinium oxysulfide, but with different densities: the standard DRZ model and the high-density PI-200 model. The Japanese-made screens can accommodate gamma-ray energies of up to approximately 500 kiloelectron volts (keV). For gamma-ray imaging, the team tested two isotopes: iridium-192, with an average energy of approximately 320 keV and a half-life of 74 days, and selenium-75, with an average energy of approximately 280 keV and a longer half-life of 120 days. Half-life has practical implications: the radiation emitted by the source decreases by half over each half-life, requiring twice the exposure time to obtain an image. Since exposures take only seconds, extending the imaging time is manageable and reduces the need to replace the source frequently. The tests showed that X-rays produced images with good sharpness and contrast. Gamma-ray images from both iridium-192 and selenium-75 were less sharp and had lower contrast but were still clear enough to detect concealed objects inside bags and parcels. The team tested a range of objects, including parcels containing mixed items such as scissors, staplers, and a tennis ball with coins hidden inside. Other test objects included a steel pipe containing stones and steel pieces with concealed drilled holes. In every case, the images revealed the internal shapes clearly enough to determine whether further inspection was needed. Social Impact and Next Steps According to Assoc. Prof. Nares this research addresses two connected needs in Thai society. The first concerns the safety of the general public. With uncertainty about the contents of parcels delivered each day, affordable screening equipment accessible to schools, government offices, and private delivery companies could help reduce the risks posed by concealed dangerous objects. The second concerns the economic benefits. Producing such equipment locally at a fraction of the cost of imported systems would lower costs and give organizations with limited budgets greater access to security screening technology. "Several organizations have already contacted us asking for advice on developing the equipment. Our team is happy to offer guidance or training so that interested organizations can build their own devices, rather than focusing solely on manufacturing them for sale. We believe sharing knowledge will make this technology more widely accessible." – Assoc. Prof. Nares "Some Thai companies have now begun producing key components such as X-ray tubes. With continued support, this could help reduce reliance on imports over the long term," Assoc. Prof. Nares said. He added that, for researchers, the satisfaction of developing an innovation comes from seeing the knowledge and technology passed on and put to good use, rather than selling as many devices as possible. "The best research is research that is put into practice and helps solve society's problems sustainably", he emphasized. Looking ahead, he sees potential applications beyond detecting firearms and ammunition, particularly in food safety screening. These could include detecting foreign materials in food products—a risk that he believes still receives too little public attention. In conclusion, the Chula Team presents this simple, low-cost X-ray imaging device consisting of a phosphor screen, a mirror, a digital camera and an L-shape plywood box. This innovation shows that meeting society's needs does not always require expensive, cutting-edge technology. Sometimes, the answer lies in thoughtfully combining basic nuclear engineering knowledge with readily available equipment. bd.title: GENIUS MACHINERY to Showcase Energy-Saving DWX Film Recycling System at IPF Japan 2026
bd.description: Designed for film recycling, the single-motor DWX targets labor shortages and rising power costs, with energy cost savings of up to 65%. TAICHUNG, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GENIUS MACHINERY, a Taiwan-based manufacturer of plastic recycling equipment, will exhibit its DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine—a compact, all-in-one system specifically engineered for plastic film recycling—at IPF Japan 2026, held from December 1 to 5 at Makuhari Messe in Chiba (Hall 7, Booth 71814). GENIUS will co-exhibit with its long-term Japanese distributor, Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd., and display the DWX system alongside film samples before and after squeezing to demonstrate its dewatering efficiency and volume reduction firsthand. GENIUS DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine for plastic film recycling. Plastic recyclers in Japan—and across most global markets—are facing mounting operational pressures on two fronts: severe labor shortages and continuously rising electricity and fuel costs. For plant operators processing agricultural film, LDPE/HDPE film, and post-consumer flexible packaging, the critical challenge is maintaining high throughput with fewer operators and lower power consumption. To address this, GENIUS developed the DWX series specifically for film applications by combining squeezing and extrusion into a single, compact unit driven by one motor and one screw. Watch the DWX squeezing and extrusion process. Crucially, the DWX retains the core dewatering mechanism of GENIUS's established DW Series Squeeze Dryer—a proven system with over 55 units sold in Japan and widely trusted by local recyclers for years. In existing Japanese post-consumer film operations, the standalone DW technology has consistently reduced outlet moisture from 50% to below 1%, cutting pellet reject rates from 15–20% to under 1%. By integrating this field-proven squeezing stage directly before extrusion, the DWX reduces washed film moisture from over 50% to below 1% in the first stage before feeding it directly into the extruder. This streamlined single-heat process helps avoid repeated melting cycles, reducing thermal degradation of the polymer while avoiding unnecessary energy and resource waste. While upfront equipment price is a one-time expense, ongoing electricity and labor bills are what truly dictate a recycling plant's long-term profitability. That is why GENIUS urges recyclers to look past the initial price tag and evaluate the total cost of ownership. In a recent line-configuration assessment for a Western European PE film recycling group, switching from a traditional three-machine setup (432 kW total installed main-motor power) to a single DWX-3512 class configuration (150 kW) would cut electricity use by an estimated 107,000 kWh a month—based on 24-hour operation, 22 days a month at 80% load and a 0.9 power factor. Overall, GENIUS estimates that the DWX series can deliver energy cost savings of up to 65%, with one to two operators able to manage the entire line. (Note: Actual savings vary depending on local electricity rates, material types, initial moisture, and throughput.) "Japanese recyclers are among the most quality-conscious in the world, and they demand verifiable performance rather than mere estimates," said Peter Tsai, CEO of GENIUS MACHINERY. "By building the DWX directly on the proven dewatering core of our DW series, we are giving film recyclers a reliable way to cut power bills and simplify staffing without compromising pellet quality. We invite visitors to our booth at IPF Japan to inspect the machine and verify our numbers line by line." Visitors to Hall 7, Booth 71814 can consult directly with technical specialists from GENIUS MACHINERY and Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd. for customized cost-of-ownership evaluations and material testing. About GENIUS MACHINERY Founded in 1975 and headquartered in Taichung, Taiwan, GENIUS MACHINERY specializes in plastic recycling machinery. Its product lineup—including the DW Plastic Squeeze Dryer and the DWX Squeeze Dryer Integrated Recycling Machine—processes agricultural film, post-consumer film, and flexible packaging waste. With over 2,000 installations across 50 countries, GENIUS provides localized sales and technical support in Japan through Zoryu Gijutsu Co., Ltd. bd.title: SHARP unveils New 15-Place Setting Dishwasher with 4-Tick Water Efficiency, Giving Modern Homes More Space, More Sparkle and More Time
bd.description: The new SHARP dishwasher QW-FP15F3A-S-B pairs generous capacity with highest Singapore 4 Ticks Water Efficiency rating, features Automatic Door Open, Dual Zone Wash and a stainless steel tub in a sleek black finish SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SHARP, the renowned leader in Japan quality & product innovation, today introduces its new 15-place setting Dishwasher (QW-FP15F3A-S-B). It is designed for homeowners who have put real thought into their space and want every appliance to feel at home in it. Finished in black, the dishwasher sits neatly alongside modern kitchen cabinetry. It also takes on the daily chore of washing up, so that evenings can go to dinner with friends, a workout or a quiet night in. Many homeowners face a trade-off when choosing a dishwasher: a larger capacity usually means higher water use. The new SHARP Dishwasher is built to avoid that compromise. It holds 15 place settings, more than the 12 to 14 typical of dishwashers in this class, yet it has earned 4 ticks in Singapore's Water Efficiency Label, using just 10.5 litres of water per cycle. Better Than the Kitchen Tap: Water, Hygiene and Time Switching from hand-washing to a full-size dishwasher brings gains on three fronts. Far less water. The dishwasher recirculates water, filtering and spraying the same water repeatedly, so a full 15-place setting load needs only about 10.5 litres per cycle in Eco mode. Washing the same load by hand under a running tap can use an estimated 60 litres. For maximum savings, users can even scrape food scraps into the bin instead of pre-rinsing plates at the tap before loading. A more hygienic clean. Hands can only comfortably tolerate tap water of around 40°C to 45°C, which isn't hot enough to tackle common household bacteria. The dishwasher heats water internally to up to 60°C in Intensive mode, helping remove stubborn grease, germs and bacteria. It also removes the need for kitchen sponges and damp cloths, which can harbour bacteria. After the wash, Automatic Door Open vents moisture so dishes dry properly, which limits the damp conditions where mould and microbes thrive. Hours back every week. Loading and unloading a 15-place setting machine takes roughly 10 to 15 minutes of active effort a day, far less than washing the same volume of plates, bowls, cutlery and cookware by hand at the sink. Dirty dishes can go straight into the machine through the day, so the sink and drying rack stay clear and the kitchen looks as good as the day it was designed. Room for Everything, From Weekend Hosting to Everyday Dinners The 15-place setting capacity lets households clear the sink in fewer loads, and thoughtful details make every load easier to arrange: Third Cutlery Rack: The dedicated top rack holds over 13 sets of metal tableware and expands loading capacity, freeing up the lower racks for plates, bowls and pots. Easy Lift-up Device: The upper rack can be raised to fit non-standard tableware of different sizes, so tall glasses and oversized platters don't have to be left behind. Interior LED Lighting: Top and front-mounted LED lights illuminate the tub in dim conditions, making loading and unloading clear and effortless, even for late-night clean-ups. Smart Savings: Less Water, Less Energy, Less Worry Auto Washing: A dirtiness sensor detects how soiled the water is during the wash and adjusts the cycle duration accordingly, so each load gets what it needs and nothing more. Half Load Wash / Dual Zone Wash: For smaller loads, users can place dishes in a single zone to activate just one spray arm, lowering both water and electricity use compared with running a standard cycle for a half-empty tub. Automatic Door Open: After washing, the door opens by 10 cm to vent moisture. This improves energy efficiency and reduces running time by 12.7% compared with residual temperature drying. At just 1.72 kWh per cycle, and operating at a quiet 47 dBA, the dishwasher can run unobtrusively in open-plan homes, whether during dinner, during a work-from-home call or overnight. Flexible Programmes for Every Kind of Day. Design That Completes the Home The dishwasher's stainless steel tub and filter offer superior durability, corrosion resistance and easy cleaning compared with standard plastic filters. They also resist discolouration, deformation and ageing, so the dishwasher looks and performs like new for longer. For households with young children, the Child Lock adds peace of mind. With eight washing programmes, the dishwasher fits the rhythm of any lifestyle: Intensive, ECO, Light, Auto, 90 min, 60 min, Rapid and Pre-Rinse. The 1–24 hour Delay Start lets users set the wash to finish when it suits them, such as in the morning before leaving for work or during off-peak hours. Dishes are clean and ready by the time the day begins. Finished in black, with button controls and a compact footprint of 600 x 850 x 600 mm, the SHARP Dishwasher is designed to blend into kitchens that have been carefully planned and styled. ae.title: Chengdu: Where poetry flows through everyday life
ae.description: BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A report from People's Daily -- German poet and painter Margarete Werner reads at home. (Photo/Dai Guangyu) The Minjiang River has carved its path through the landscape for millennia, but it was human ingenuity that truly tamed it. The Dujiangyan irrigation system, engineered over two thousand years ago in southwest China's Sichuan province, channels the river's waters across the fertile Chengdu Plain. For centuries, this marvel of hydraulic engineering has shielded the region from catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, laying the foundation for what became known as the "Land of Abundance." Long before modern infrastructure, Sichuan attracted scholars and poets, earning the enduring belief that the land itself inspires verse. Chengdu holds a rare distinction in Chinese history: it has occupied the same site and kept the same name for roughly three thousand years. Today, it stands as a living testament to this continuity -- a metropolis where deep-rooted traditions and dynamic innovation thrive side by side. Nestled among the misty peaks of Qingcheng Mountain, a quiet cottage belongs to Margarete Werner, a German painter and poet who goes by the Chinese name Lei Zhen. Inside, floor-to-ceiling shelves hold Chinese classics alongside Western literary works, reflecting a mind shaped by two cultures. Surrounded by emerald hills and terraced tea gardens, she finds inspiration at the intersection of Eastern and Western thought. Werner grew up in the foothills of the Alps. Ink and wash paintings collected by her grandmother first introduced her to the aesthetics of the East. At 19, while studying in London, she happened upon Chinese classics in a bookstore in Chinatown. From then on, she felt drawn to this distant land. After graduation, she moved to China, eventually settling on Qingcheng Mountain with her husband to focus fully on her writing. "I've always felt that Li Bai is a profoundly universal poet. His verses speak directly to the human experience, transcending time and borders," she said. She often recites poetry while hiking mountain trails. One line from Li Bai's Dulu Pian resonates deeply with her: "A bright moon shines straight down, revealing all without concealment." Its unguarded honesty mirrors the tranquil, grounded life she has cultivated here. Sichuan has long had a close connection with poetry. Famous Chinese poets Du Fu, Li Bai, and Lu You all composed celebrated works in Chengdu, helping shape the city's cultural character. For Werner, however, the city's poetic spirit is not confined to the pages of books. It is also alive in everyday speech. Residents still use words like luo yu (falling rain) and niao huan (birds singing), preserving the musicality of ancient Chinese in daily conversation. "Standing at the foot of Qingcheng Mountain, I feel that the rhythms of Tang and Song poetry have returned to their original form," Werner said. This poetic atmosphere extends beyond literature. Since the launch of the Chengdu International Poetry Week in 2017, more than 110 foreign poets from over 50 countries and regions have visited the city to seek inspiration. Their works offer glimpses of Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets, with some featured in a collection titled "A city in the depths of time: Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets." To Werner, "poetry is like green bamboo, with the vitality to pierce through concrete."

sa.title: صقّار قطري: مهرجان الملك عبدالعزيز للصقور أهم مسابقة للصقور في العالم
sa.description: رسّخ مهرجان الملك عبدالعزيز للصقور مكانته الدولية، بوصفه أكبر تجمع للصقور في العالم، ووجهة للصقارين المحترفين من مختلف الدول، بما يحظى به من مستوى تنافسي وتنظيمي جعله يتصدر مسابقات الصقور عالميًا. وأكد الصقار القطري ناصر علي الحميدي، الذي يشارك في مسابقة الملواح ضمن فئة المحترفين الدوليين، أن مهرجان الملك عبدالعزيز للصقور يُعد أهم مسابقة للصقور على مستوى العالم. وأضاف أن المكانة العالمية التي بلغها المهرجان، وتصدره مسابقات الصقور يمثلان إنجازًا يستحق الإشادة، ويشكلان دافعًا له للحرص على المشاركة في منافساته. شغف كبير بالمشاركة وأوضح الحميدي أن مشاركته في المهرجان هذا العام امتداد لمشاركته في الأعوام السابقة، إذ تُوّج بكأس الملك عبدالعزيز في عامي 2024 و2025 ضمن فئة المحترفين الدوليين. وأشار إلى أنه تنقل بين دولة قطر والمملكة العربية السعودية لتدريب صقوره وإعدادها للمشاركة في المهرجان، لافتًا إلى أنه أمضى نحو شهر في المملكة استعدادًا للمشاركة، والاستفادة من الأجواء الملائمة لتدريب الصقور. وعن علاقته بالصقارة، أفاد الحميدي بأن شغفه بها بدأ منذ طفولته، إذ نشأ في أسرة توارثت ممارسة الصقارة جيلًا بعد جيل، وتعلّم أصولها من والده، مضيفًا أن الصقارة تمثل إرثًا عائليًا متوارثًا يحرص على المحافظة عليه. مهرجان الملك عبدالعزيز للصقور 2026 يُذكر أن مهرجان الملك عبدالعزيز للصقور 2026، الذي ينظمه المركز الوطني للصقور في مقره بمَلهم شمال مدينة الرياض، يستمر حتى 30 نوفمبر الجاري، بمشاركة صقارين محليين ودوليين يتنافسون في 140 شوطًا ضمن مسابقتي الملواح والمزاين، على جوائز مالية وألقاب كؤوس الملك عبدالعزيز و"سيف الملك" و"شلفا الملك".

iq.title: "غير صالحة للسكن".. أدخنة المعامل وتصريحات البيئة تحاصر بسماية
iq.description: شفق نيوز- بغداد على بعد نحو 25 كيلومتراً من مركز العاصمة بغداد، تواجه مدينة بسماية السكنية أزمة بيئية متفاقمة، مع تصاعد شكاوى سكانها من الأدخنة والروائح المنبعثة من المعامل المحيطة بها، وما تثيره من مخاوف بشأن التداعيات الصحية على عشرات الآلاف من المواطنين، وهي مخاوف زادتها تصريحات وزيرة البيئة التي وصفت فيها المجمع بأنه "غير صالح للسكن". وأُطلق مشروع بسماية، الواقع جنوب شرقي بغداد على الطريق الدولي الرابط بالعاصمة ومحافظة واسط، عام 2012، بوصفه أحد أكبر مشاريع الإسكان في العراق، ونُفذ بالتعاقد مع شركة "هانوا" الكورية الجنوبية، فيما بدأت أعمال البناء عام 2013، وكان من المتوقع استقبال السكان عام 2015، قبل تسليم الدفعات الأولى من الوحدات السكنية في نيسان/ أبريل 2016. وصُمم المشروع ليكون مدينة متكاملة تضم 100 ألف وحدة سكنية، بطاقة استيعابية تصل إلى 600 ألف نسمة، لكن وجود معامل الطابوق والأسفلت ومصادر التلوث في محيطه بات يثير مخاوف متزايدة بشأن ملاءمة بيئته للسكن. وتجدد الجدل عقب تصريحات وزيرة البيئة العراقية سروة عبد الواحد، خلال مقابلة تلفزيونية في 15 تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر الجاري، أكدت فيها أن مجمع بسماية "غير صالح للسكن"، وأن الوزارة لم تمنحه موافقات بيئية بسبب وجود المعامل والأنشطة الملوثة في المنطقة، مشيرة إلى أن مجمع الورد في منطقة النهروان لن يحصل على إجازة للسبب ذاته. وأثارت تصريحات الوزيرة تساؤلات بشأن حقيقة الموافقات البيئية التي حصل عليها المشروع قبل إنشائه، ولا سيما أن الهيئة الوطنية للاستثمار كانت قد أعلنت، خلال مراحل إطلاقه، حصوله على الموافقات الأصولية من الوزارات المعنية، بما فيها وزارة البيئة، التي أشارت حينها إلى سلامة الموقع وخلوه من التلوث. ورداً على تصريحات الوزيرة، قال المتحدث الرسمي باسم الهيئة الوطنية للاستثمار، سلام الربيعي، لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن منح الإجازات الاستثمارية يخضع بشكل صارم لضوابط قانون الاستثمار رقم (13) لسنة 2006 وتعديلاته. وأضاف أن مشروع مدينة بسماية الجديدة مُنح إجازته الاستثمارية استناداً إلى تلك الضوابط وقرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (152) لسنة 2012، وبعد استكمال موافقات جميع الجهات القطاعية ذات العلاقة، وفي مقدمتها موافقة وزارة البيئة لإقامة المشروع. وشدد الربيعي على حرص الهيئة والتزامها بمطابقة جميع المشاريع الاستثمارية للمعايير والاشتراطات البيئية المعتمدة، ولا سيما المشاريع السكنية، مؤكداً أنها لا تتوانى، ضمن حدود صلاحياتها، عن مخاطبة الجهات الرقابية المعنية لاتخاذ الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة بحق أي مخالفات بيئية قد تُرصد. وعلى وقع الجدل بشأن التلوث والاستياء الذي أثارته تصريحاتها، تحركت وزيرة البيئة سروة عبد الواحد ميدانياً، أمس الأربعاء، بالتعاون مع دائرة العمليات في وزارة الداخلية وقيادة طيران الجيش، لتنفيذ جولة جوية فوق بغداد ومحيطها، بهدف رصد بؤر التلوث ومصادر الانبعاثات. وبحسب بيان صدر عن مكتبها، أسفرت الجولة، التي شملت معسكر الرشيد وبسماية والنهروان، عن تشخيص عشرات الأنشطة المخالفة، فيما وجهت الوزيرة باتخاذ إجراءات قانونية رادعة بحق الملوثين، وعدم الاكتفاء بالإنذارات. وشددت عبد الواحد على أن الرقابة البيئية ستتواصل جواً وأرضاً، وأن لا جهة فوق القانون، ولا مساومة على صحة المواطنين، وفق تعبيرها. أدخنة وشكاوى وعلى الأرض، يشكو سكان في بسماية من تصاعد نشاط المعامل المحيطة بالمدينة خلال الفترة الأخيرة، وما يصاحبه من انتشار الأدخنة والروائح، خصوصاً خلال ساعات الليل وحتى الصباح. ويشير السكان إلى أن الجهات المختصة كانت تنفذ، خلال السنوات الماضية، جولات تفتيشية على المعامل، تتخللها إنذارات وإجراءات بحق المخالفين، ما دفع بعض المنشآت إلى تقليص ساعات عملها، إلا أنهم يلاحظون تراجع تلك الإجراءات، مقابل استمرار تشغيل معامل لساعات طويلة، وأحياناً على مدار 24 ساعة. ويقول عدد من الأهالي إن الأدخنة تبدأ بالانتشار منذ ساعات الليل الأولى، وتزداد خلال الفجر والصباح، بالتزامن مع خروج الموظفين والطلبة إلى أعمالهم ومدارسهم، فيما تتسبب الروائح المنبعثة بحالة من الضيق والقلق بين السكان. وفي مناشدة، دعا صباح الكعبي، أحد سكان بسماية، وزيرة البيئة إلى التدخل العاجل لوضع حد لمعاناة الأهالي جراء تلوث الهواء، محذراً من انعكاساته المحتملة على صحة المواطنين، ولا سيما الأطفال وكبار السن. وطالب الكعبي، عبر مواقع التواصل، باتخاذ إجراءات فعلية للحد من مصادر التلوث ومحاسبة الجهات المتسببة به، داعياً سكان المدينة إلى تنظيم وقفة احتجاجية سلمية لإيصال مطالبهم إلى المؤسسات الحكومية، ومؤكداً أن حقهم في العيش ضمن بيئة آمنة وهواء نظيف لا يحتمل التأجيل. من جانبها، تتساءل فرح عبدو، وهي من سكان المدينة، عن مصير المجمعات السكنية الأخرى القريبة من المناطق الصناعية، مشيرة إلى مجمع الورد في النهروان، فضلاً عن مناطق سكنية في حي الوحدة والنهر وغيرها. وتقول عبدو إن التصريحات تثير تساؤلات بشأن آلية منح الموافقات للمشاريع السكنية في مناطق تحيط بها الأنشطة الصناعية، مضيفة أن المسؤولية تقتضي وجود تنسيق مسبق بين الوزارات والجهات المعنية قبل السماح بإنشاء تلك المشاريع. أما معتز آل محمود، أحد الناشطين في بسماية، فيصف التلوث بأنه خطر لا يمكن الاستهانة به، محذراً من أن آثاره الصحية قد لا تظهر بالضرورة بصورة فورية، وإنما قد تتكشف بعد سنوات. ويقول آل محمود إن روائح الكبريت باتت تثير قلق الأهالي، مشيراً إلى تسجيل حالات إعياء بين بعض السكان عقب استنشاقها، ومطالباً بتحرك جدي للحد من الانبعاثات ومحاسبة الجهات المتسببة بها. ويستحضر في هذا السياق قراراً سابقاً لرئيس الوزراء علي الزيدي بمنح المعامل الموجودة في المنطقة مهلة عام لإزالتها ونقلها، معتبراً أن تنفيذ القرار بات ضرورة ملحة، وأن مواجهة المشكلة تتطلب تحركاً جماعياً من سكان بسماية وقضاء المدائن عموماً. تداخل المسؤوليات وفي قراءة لأبعاد الأزمة، يرى الكاتب والإعلامي سالم مشكور أن مصادر التلوث في محيط بسماية لا تقتصر على معامل الطابوق والأسفلت، بل تشمل أيضاً أفران صهر المعادن ومحارق النفايات العشوائية، محذراً من تداعياتها الصحية على سكان المدينة والمناطق القريبة، وصولاً إلى جرف النداف. ويقول مشكور لوكالة شفق نيوز إن المشكلة تتفاقم في ظل غياب تحرك حكومي منسق، ومحاولة كل جهة إلقاء المسؤولية على الأخرى، مؤكداً أن الأولوية يجب أن تكون لمعالجة التلوث وحماية السكان، بدلاً من تبادل الاتهامات بشأن الجهات التي منحت الموافقات للمشروع. ويشير إلى أن توسع المدن يفرض على الحكومات مسؤولية نقل المعامل والأنشطة الصناعية الملوثة بعيداً عن المناطق السكنية، لافتاً إلى أن عدداً من المنشآت المخالفة للشروط البيئية يعمل خلال ساعات الليل، ما يستدعي تشديد الرقابة ومحاسبة المتسببين. ولا يستبعد مشكور وجود جهات نافذة توفر الحماية لبعض المعامل المخالفة، معتبراً أن استمرار الانبعاثات رغم المناشدات يستدعي تدخلاً استثنائياً من رئيس الوزراء علي الزيدي، عبر تنسيق جهود الوزارات والمؤسسات المعنية وإسنادها بالقوى الأمنية لمنع أي تدخل يحول دون محاسبة المنشآت المخالفة وفرض الإجراءات اللازمة بحقها. رقابة ميدانية في المقابل، تؤكد مديرية شرطة حماية البيئة وجود مفارز تفتيشية نهارية وليلية لمراقبة الأنشطة الصناعية ومصادر التلوث في محيط بسماية والنهروان، مشيرة إلى إغلاق عدد من معامل الأسفلت والطابوق المخالفة. ويقول مدير المديرية التابعة لوزارة الداخلية، اللواء ثائر حميد صالح، لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن المفارز نفذت إجراءات رقابية على معامل الأسفلت المؤكسد والطابوق في منطقة النهروان، وأسفرت عن إغلاق عدد منها، في إطار الحد من الأنشطة الملوثة. لكنه يلفت إلى وجود مشكلة أخرى تتمثل بموقع الطمر الصحي في النهروان، وما يرتبط به من مخاطر حرق النفايات وانبعاث الغازات، ومنها غاز الميثان المتراكم في مواقع الطمر، مشدداً على حاجة هذا الملف إلى تدخل وجهد كبيرين من أمانة بغداد. ويشير صالح إلى أن مسؤولية الأمانة تتضمن عزل النفايات وإعادة تدويرها والحد من عمليات الحرق، فيما تواصل شرطة البيئة مراقبة هذه الأنشطة ومتابعة المخالفات. أما بشأن قياس مستويات تلوث الهواء والتأكد من مطابقتها للمعايير البيئية والصحية، فيوضح أن هذه المهمة تقع ضمن اختصاص قسم مراقبة جودة الهواء في وزارة البيئة، الذي يمتلك متحسسات في بؤر التلوث لقياس مستويات الانبعاثات وتحديد مدى مطابقتها للمحددات المعتمدة. وفي سياق متصل، أكد مرصد "العراق الأخضر" البيئي، في وقت سابق من اليوم الأحد، استمرار تلوث الهواء في بغداد بسبب الإجراءات غير المجدية للجهات المعنية بملف الأنشطة المخالفة للمحددات البيئية في العاصمة، واصفاً التصريحات الرسمية بشأن إيقاف تلك الأنشطة بأنها "غير صحيحة". وكان المرصد قد كشف، في وقت سابق، عن ضعف الرقابة البيئية على الأنشطة الصناعية والاستثمارية في العاصمة بغداد، مشيراً إلى أنها تتسبب في ارتفاع مستويات التلوث في بعض مناطقها. والعام الماضي، احتلت بغداد المرتبة الثانية عالمياً في قائمة أكثر المدن تلوثاً بالهواء، بحسب بيانات منصة IQAir السويسرية المتخصصة بمراقبة جودة الهواء. وفي ختام جولتها الميدانية، وثقت عدسة وكالة شفق نيوز واقع مدينة بسماية والأجواء المحيطة بها، كما زارت عدداً من المعامل القريبة من المدينة، ورصدت تصاعد أعمدة الدخان والانبعاثات الناجمة عن أنشطتها، وما تسببه من تلوث في المنطقة، في مشهد يعكس حجم التحديات البيئية التي تواجه سكان المدينة.
